Fisher tutorial

The Fisher matrix can be calculated using the function DALITensors. Its inputs are the waveform model, the source parameters, the detector network and the order for DALI tensors. Since we want the Fisher matrix, we will set the order to 1. The output is the Fisher matrix of the network.

DALITensors[Appr, fp, {det1, det2, ...}, 1]

Calculates the Fisher matrix for the waveform model Appr, with source parameters fp, and the detector network {det1, det2, ...}.

Parameters

Appr: Waveform model. Supported values are "IMRPhenomD" and "IMRPhenomHM".

fp: Association containing the source parameters.

{det1, det2, ...}: List of associations representing the detectors in the network.

Returns

The Fisher matrix of the detector network.

The convention for fp follows section Fiducial point and the convention for deti follows section Detector association.

Example

The following example calculates the Fisher matrix using the IMRPhenomD waveform model:

fp = <|
    "dec" -> 3.14/2, "phi" -> 3.4, "psi" -> 0.1,
    "Mc" -> 0.0116, "q" -> 0.2,
    "s1z" -> 0.1, "s2z" -> 0.1,
    "iota" -> 2.5, "invdL" -> 1, "tc" -> 10, "phiRef" -> 0.
|>;

H1 = <|
    "Position" -> DetectorVertex["H1"],
    "DetectorTensor" -> DetectorTensor["H1"],
    "ASD" -> ASD["L1H1-O5"]
|>;

L1 = <|
    "Position" -> DetectorVertex["L1"],
    "DetectorTensor" -> DetectorTensor["L1"],
    "ASD" -> ASD["L1H1-O5"]
|>;

FM = DALITensors["IMRPhenomD", fp, {H1, L1}, 1];

We note that FM has dimensions {1,1,121}:

Dimensions[FM]
 {1, 1, 121}

If we want the familiar matrix dimensions we can use

FM2 = ArrayReshape[FM, {11, 11}];

To invert the Fisher matrix we can use the CholeskyInverse function:

{Cov, epsilon} = CholeskyInverse[FM2];

Cov is the Fisher inverse calculated through a Cholesky decomposition. epsilon is the error on the inversion. We defined epsilon, following 2207.02771, to be the largest error between the product of the Fisher matrix and its inverse with respect to the identity:

diff1 = FM2.Cov - IdentityMatrix[11]//Abs;
diff2 = Cov.FM2- IdentityMatrix[11]//Abs;
epsilon = Max[{diff1, diff2}];

The recommendation is that epsilon should be less than 0.05.

The derivatives that are used to calculate the Fisher matrix are with respect to the variables in fp. Their order, that is which variable corresponds to which dimension, can be accessed through the function EmptyAssociation. For example, the following code gives us the exact correspondence between waveform variables and matrix dimensions:

EmptyAssociation["Aligned"]
<|
    "dec" -> 1, "phi" -> 2, "psi" -> 3, "Mc" -> 4,
    "q" -> 5, "s1z" -> 6, "s2z" -> 7, "iota" -> 8, "invdL" -> 9,
    "tc" -> 10, "phiRef" -> 11
|>

Options

The function also accepts options to specify the frequency range, resolution and whether to return the Fisher matrix of each detector separately. The default settings are shown below:

FM = DALITensors[
    "IMRPhenomD", fp, {H1, L1}, 1,
    "fmin" -> 20, "fmax" -> 1024, "res" -> 1000,
    "AllFisherMatrices" -> False
];

When AllFisherMatrices is set to True, the output will be a list of the previous output form:

FM = DALITensors[
    "IMRPhenomD", fp, {H1, L1}, 1,
    "fmin" -> 20, "fmax" -> 1024, "res" -> 1000,
    "AllFisherMatrices" -> True
];
Dimensions[FM]
 {2, 1, 1, 121}

The order of Fisher matrices is the same of the detector network, in this case {H1, L1}.

For the IMRPhenomD model is possible to calculate the Fisher matrix with derivatives of the waveform on TIGER parameters:

\[\left(\delta \varphi_{-2}, \, \delta \varphi_{0}, \delta \varphi_{1}, \delta \varphi_{2}, \delta \varphi_{3}, \delta \varphi_{4}, \delta \varphi_{5l}, \delta \varphi_{6}, \delta \varphi_{6l}, \delta \varphi_{7} \right)\]

The way of including these extra parameters is passing them as additional keys for the fiducial point association. For instance

 fp = <|
    "dec" -> 3.14/2, "phi" -> 3.4, "psi" -> 0.1,
    "Mc" -> 0.0116, "q" -> 0.2,
    "s1z" -> 0.1, "s2z" -> 0.1,
    "iota" -> 2.5, "invdL" -> 1, "tc" -> 10, "phiRef" -> 0.,
    "\[Delta]\[CurlyPhi]0" -> 0
|>;

when passed to DALITensors will include derivatives of \(\delta \varphi_0\). The variable \(\delta \varphi_0\) will correspond to the dimension 12 of the Fisher matrix, keeping the relation of GR variables and dimension intact. You can pass more than one parameter:

 fp = <|
    "dec" -> 3.14/2, "phi" -> 3.4, "psi" -> 0.1,
    "Mc" -> 0.0116, "q" -> 0.2,
    "s1z" -> 0.1, "s2z" -> 0.1,
    "iota" -> 2.5, "invdL" -> 1, "tc" -> 10, "phiRef" -> 0.,
     "\[Delta]\[CurlyPhi]2" -> 0, "\[Delta]\[CurlyPhi]0" -> 0
|>;

In which case \(\delta \varphi_0\) will correspond to the dimension 12 and \(\delta \varphi_2\) to the dimension 13. The ordering is defined by the sequence

\[\left(\delta \varphi_{-2}, \, \delta \varphi_{0}, \delta \varphi_{1}, \delta \varphi_{2}, \delta \varphi_{3}, \delta \varphi_{4}, \delta \varphi_{5l}, \delta \varphi_{6}, \delta \varphi_{6l}, \delta \varphi_{7} \right)\]

lower numbers will always correspond to lower dimensions. The syntax for all TIGER parameters is the same of Options[hphcIMRPhenomD].
